title: Card Relationship Levels That Narrow the Temporary Credit Standing on Personal Checking
content:
The temporary credit standing on a Personal Checking account is narrowed in two cases, read from the owner's record under Personal Credit Cards and from a premier money market balance held under Savings & Money Market Accounts.

**First case.** Where the owner has made at least 10 card payments in the last twelve months and a temporary credit entry stands on the account, only the temporary credit entries posted inside the claim window are summed, still less every take-back entry already booked. The claim window runs back 2 calendar months from the day the matter is handled.

**Second case.** Where the case above does not apply and either the owner has made at least 4 card payments in the last twelve months or the owner's premier money market balance reaches the protection source minimum of 5000.00, only the largest single temporary credit entry is taken.

**Otherwise.** Where neither case applies, the temporary credit standing is not narrowed in either of these ways.

**Worked narrowing on hypothetical inputs.** An account carries temporary credit entries of 120.00 and 90.00 posted inside the claim window and one of 200.00 posted five months ago, with 40.00 of take-back entries already booked.

| Owner's position | Temporary credit standing |
|---|---|
| 11 card payments in the last twelve months, a temporary credit entry standing | 170.00, being the 210.00 posted inside the claim window less the 40.00 already taken back |
| 6 card payments in the last twelve months | 200.00, being the largest single temporary credit entry |
| 1 card payment, premier money market balance of 7000.00 | 200.00, the premier money market limb of the second case being met |
| 1 card payment, premier money market balance of 300.00 | Neither case applies |

The first case requires both of its limbs; the second is met by either limb alone. Under the first case the take-back entries already booked are still deducted; under the second they are not, the largest single entry being taken as it stands. Equality satisfies each threshold, so exactly 10 card payments reaches the first case and exactly 4 reaches the card limb of the second.
